chunks: What was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
There is no harm in performing the later evening prayer earlier during travel before the twilight disappears.

key_terms.الشَّفَقُ: the twilight glow that remains after sunset
key_terms.عِشَاءَ الْآخِرَةِ: the ʿIshāʾ prayer, the later evening salat
key_terms.فِي السَّفَرِ: during travel; in the state of journeying
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; an expression indicating permissibility
key_terms.يَغِيبَ: to disappear or go out of sight
key_terms.يُعَجِّلَ: to bring forward or perform earlier than the usual time

ai.seo_question: Can a traveler perform ʿIshāʾ before the twilight disappears?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal concession for a traveler regarding the timing of the ʿIshāʾ prayer. It states that in travel, there is no harm in advancing the later evening prayer before the disappearance of the twilight, indicating ease in worship during travel.
